chapters.headline: POETICAL
chapters.text: First up — Page 1, Column 1. POETICAL. The following sublime ode to the Deity, is from the Russian Anthology, and was written by the celebrated DERZHAVEN. This poem is said to have been translated into Japanese, by order of the Emperor, and hung up embroidered in gold in the temple of Jeddo. It has also been translated into the Chinese and Tartar languages, written on a piece of rich silk, and suspended in the imperial palace at Pekin. It was translated into English, as follows, by Dr. BOWRING, and is said to have lost much of its original beauty by the translation. It is a noble composition, and should be preserved or committed to memory by every reader of the Sentinel.

chapters.headline: GOD
chapters.text:
GOD. Opening stanzas actually present:
O thou eternal One! whose presence bright
All space doth occupy, all motion guide;
Unchanged through times's all devastating flight,
Thou only God! There is no God beside!
Being above all beings! Mighty One!
Whom none can comprehend and none explore;
Who fill'st existence with Thyself alone:
Embracing all,--supporting--ruling o'er--
Being whom we call God--and know no more!
It its sublime research, philosophy
May measure out the ocean deep--may count
The sands or the sun's rays--but God! for Thee
There is no weight nor measure:--none can mount
Up to Thy mysteries. Reason's brightest spark,
Though kindled by Thy light, in vain would try
To trace Thy counsels, infinite and dark,
And thought is lost ere thought can soar so high--
E'en like past moments in eternity.
The ode continues through later stanzas (creation from nothing; suns born as sparks; the unmeasured universe). A short filler joke at the foot of the column: "John," said a girl to her beau...

chapters.headline: MISCELLANEOUS
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 1, Column 2. MISCELLANEOUS. The following beautiful description of a blind preacher is from the Hon. Wm. Wirt. The sketch has been selected by the Rev. Timothy Flint and published in his series of essays contributed to the London Athenaeum, on American literature, as the finest specimen of the descriptive. Gray's "Full many a flower is born to blush unseen" is quoted. The editorial note says that but for Mr. Wirt the sermon of the blind preacher would never have been heard beyond the walls of the "ruinous, old wooden house" in the wilds of Virginia. Ed. Sentinel.
The Wirt narrative of the Virginia woods sermon occupies the rest of this column and runs into column 3.
Short jokes at the column foot (rents / breeches; "All flesh is grass"; sticking-plaster).

chapters.headline: Death of General Bertrand
chapters.text:
Death of General Bertrand. Henri Gatien Bertrand: followed Napoleon to Elba; return 20 March; after Waterloo never quitted him; exile; revolution of July; later accompanied the ashes brought by the Prince de Joinville. Died on the 31st ult. after the yellow of his long exile. Praised as a model of honesty and fidelity.
Short fillers near the foot (school-child compass points; turpentine-on-sugar for cholic appears again as a broken line).

chapters.headline: "BARGAIN AND SALE."
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 2, Columns 1-2. "BARGAIN AND SALE.". SPEECH OF MR. BALDWIN, of Clinton.
Extract from a speech of Mr. Baldwin, of Clinton county, recently delivered before the Hickory Club, Columbus. It opposes the unholy league, the "bargain and sale," entered into by the friends of Adams and Clay to defeat the election of Gen. Jackson. Mentions "old Mordecai Hartley, the Whig candidate for Governor" among those who entered into the alliance ( Shirt of Nessus image used of the charge.
Majority-have-the-right-to-rule argument; Alien and Sedition laws; Jefferson vs. Burr in the House.

chapters.headline: To the Democrats of Harrison County
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 2, Columns 4-5. To the Democrats of Harrison County. Having unexpectedly seen my name in the KAY-diz Sentinel as a candidate for nomination for the Senate and not having yet obtained my own consent to be a candidate for that or any other office... declining. Came to the county in 1842; after the resignation of the Federal members, declined to defend the Ohio banking law. Labor as the only source of wealth; bankers living on interest. Some about KAY-diz treat paper money as the centre of political action and will not vote for any man entertaining such sentiments; therefore he will not permit his name to go before them, but will not go over to the whig ranks.
Your fellow citizen,

chapters.headline: Horrible Murder
chapters.text: Horrible Murder. Reprint: Friday morning last, about 10 o'clock, George Weeks of this place, statement before W. Jones, Esq., shot a colored man named Edward. Quarrel over employment; Weeks borrowed a gun from Mr. Smith north of unclear; shot Edward at the stand of Mr. Martin. Arrested by Sheriff Simpson; true bill for murder; plea not guilty; trial in Common Pleas in June.

chapters.headline: Declinations (local)
chapters.text: Declinations (local). Mr. Editor: I see my name before the people, in your paper, for the several offices of Representative, Commissioner and Director of the Poor. Believing that there are persons in the Democratic ranks upon whom the party could more cordially unite than myself, I have concluded not to be a candidate for any of those offices.

chapters.headline: EDITED BY L. HARPER
chapters.text:
EDITED BY L. HARPER. "HE IS A FREEMAN WHOM THE TRUTH MAKES FREE."
KAY-diz, OHIO:
THURSDAY MORNING, MARCH 28, 1844.
Kind and courteous Reader! You were apprized through the columns of the Sentinel last week, that Mr. Mick GON uh gul, who has been its able editor for a long time past, had disposed of the establishment to the undersigned.
Inaugural: the paper will be a true exponent of Democratic measures; history of federalists vs. anti-federalists / Republicans (Hamilton vs. Madison); 1840 hard-cider campaign; Harrison's death; Tyler and "Tippecanoe and Tyler too"; Henry Clay as the 1844 federal candidate, travelling in the south and disturbing the sabbath.

chapters.headline: Page 3, Column 2
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 3, Column 2. Page 3, Column 2. Continuation: if federalists gain, a National Bank of fifty millions; high tariff; assumption of state debts; distribution of public-land proceeds; abolition of the veto; a host of state banks. The paper will advocate MARTIN VAN BUREN and DAVID TOD. Tod bank program restated (specie-paid stock; individual liability; issues limited to three times specie; loans to stockholders limited; penalties for fraud). No personal abuse of private individuals. Moral essays, historical sketches, biographies, an occasional tale, poetry, market notes.
Having thus given an outline... L. HARPER.

J. Mick GON uh gul,
JOHN Mick NEEL,
Executive Committee.

chapters.headline: WAS THAT THUNDER?
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 3, Column 4. WAS THAT THUNDER?. New Hampshire returns: Steele, Democratic candidate for Governor, large majority over Colby, the Clay candidate; later "over 10,000." House and Senate Democratic. Isaac Hill called a traitor / adjunct of coonery.
NEW YORK town elections Democratic. MASSACHUSETTS "going it on the loud." NEW JERSEY: Camden, John C. Cowperthwait, dem., over R. W. Howell, 48 majority.
A man in town has purchased all the 'coon skins in the region -- joke that whigs cannot revive 1840.
This paper will be sent to a number of political friends; those who do not wish to subscribe, return it. Packet book: old patrons whose "bump of payativeness" is deficient omitted.
Mr. Woodbury's speech on the Tariff, copy from Mr. Morris, member of Congress. Baltimore Jackson birthday; toast by Hon. James Buchanan.
No change in the terms of the Sentinel.
Slave trade, Havana letter 25th ult. (N. O. Bee): ship with upwards of one thousand negroes; $13,000 said paid to the Captain General.
Detroit Daily Advertiser on Mr. Clay's prospects (Harrisburg 1839; Weed; Greeley).
Ex-Governor Lucas has sold his estate in Pike county, Ohio, and is on his way to Iowa.

chapters.headline: The Stock Township Boys Awake
chapters.text:
Next up — Page 3, Column 6. The Stock Township Boys Awake. The following proceedings have been handed in for publication:
At a large and respectable meeting of the democrats of Stock township, held on the 21st inst., at the house of George Lightle, the following persons were appointed committee men in accordance with the plan for carrying out the popular vote system, viz: John Cramlet, Isaac Layport, Abraham Bargar, William Spiker, Albert West.
Sub-Committee for each School District.
No. 1. Alexander Maxwell, Hamilton McFadden, George McKinney.
No. 2. George Lightle, Robert McFadden, Samuel Brindly.
No. 3. unclear L. Crawford, John D. Wilson, John Layport.
No. 4. Stephen W. Heavlin, McCaslin unclear, William Layport.
No. 5. James T. Anderson, John Tipton, John V. Layport.
No. 6. Moses H. Conaway, Samuel Lightner, J. Palmer.
No. 7. Benjamin Sims, Jacob Ghrist, Samuel W. Heavlin.
Gen. Cass letter to the Detroit Free Press: will abide by the Baltimore Convention. Baltimore Argus organization note. Trial of Hon. John B. Weller for assault and battery on Terrence Shriver, Esq., of the Baltimore Patriot; fined $10 and costs. Pennsylvania canal open. Bank of Xenia stockholders determined to wind up (Torch Light).
